text:
maya: Quick sync — we need to lock the shipping surface for customer-managed networking on the Private distro. field teams want a small, deterministic upgrade path that preserves customer IPs and peering. Who's on this?

jordan: I'm in. main constraints: minimal agent changes, deterministic DB migration, and a rollback path.

sylvia: +1 from field. Top asks from customers today: 1) preserve VIPs across upgrades 2) clear maintenance window guidance 3) a one-button rollback.

maya: Good list. Also they want an installer flag to opt into "net-preserve" mode so ops can validate before cutover. Example we discussed:
```
./install --mode private --net-preserve=true --ip-preserve=keep
```

alejandro: Runtime/networking note: we can preserve node-level IPs if we avoid re-creating the tenant veth and keep MAC stable. That requires the agent to skip interface teardown during upgrade. Cost: ~1 engineer-week + QA.

jordan: That aligns. We'll need an integration test that reboots and asserts IPs unchanged. Add a test harness for >100 tenants to catch collisions.

devx: From DX perspective, docs must include a preflight checklist for NetOps: required routes, expected BGP state, and a validation command. Suggest adding `redwoodctl network validate --expected-peer <AS>` to the quickstart.

maya: Can we sketch launch gates? My proposal:
- Gate 1: Installer flag implemented + unit/integration tests
- Gate 2: Field-verified on 2 customers in staging for 2 maintenance windows
- Gate 3: Public docs + rollback runbook

sylvia: Field can commit to two pilots but will need a sanitised checklist for each customer. We also need a fallback model: if net-preserve fails, auto-fallback to cloud-hosted routing with an explicit consent step.

alejandro: Fallback idea: switch traffic to a regional relay while operator fixes on-prem config. Implementation: a lightweight proxy that routes outbound to Redwood-hosted egress. Risk: requires bandwidth contract.

jordan: Technical tradeoffs: preserving IPs keeps customer BGP adjacency intact but limits some automated upgrades. If we choose preservation-by-default, upgrades slower and more manual. Alternative: preserve only control-plane IPs and rotate data-plane.

maya: Decision needed: do we ship with full IP preservation (higher ops cost) or control-plane-only (faster rollout)? Thoughts by EOD?

devx: Recommend control-plane-only for v1. We can label the feature "IP-stable mode (preview)" for full preservation and gate it for customers with dedicated SRE support.

sylvia: OK from field. We'll flag high-touch customers for preview. Need comms template for customer SREs.

alejandro: I'll scope the agent change and the proxy fallback prototype. ETA: 5 workdays for prototype, 2 weeks for hardened change.

jordan: I'll own integration tests and the upgrade-playbook doc. Will add a test case matrix for ip-preserve vs control-only.

maya: Action items: @alejandro prototype proxy + agent skip-teardown plan, @jordan tests + doc, @devx quickstart CLI + validation command, @sylvia schedule two pilots, ops-bot please create a ticket for the rollout checklist.

ops-bot: Created ISSUE-PRIVNET-4123: "Private deploy network-preserve rollout checklist" assigned to maya. Link: https://redwood.internal/ISSUE-PRIVNET-4123

maya: Thanks. We'll reconvene in 48h with firm ETA and pilot customer names. :calendar:
